title: A broad early-childhood support system can coordinate programs while leaving outcome management incomplete
source_unit: GAO-26-107572, Pregnancy and Early Childhood: Performance Management Process Needed for Three Programs
geography: United States; federal programs serving pregnant women, children through age 5, or their families

observations.period: Fiscal year 2024 programs; report published May 2026

denominator.unit: federal programs and tax expenditures identified as serving pregnant women, children through age 5, or their families, among other groups

focused_programs.unit: programs providing some amount of direct services solely to the target population

agency_spread.unit: federal agencies administering the 15 focused direct-service programs

coordination.value: officials from all 15 focused programs reported coordinating with other programs serving the population
coordination.unit: program-official report, not a measure of beneficiary experience or coordination quality

performance_management_gap.value: 3 of 15 focused programs had not fully established a federal performance-management process for goals, performance information, and results assessment
performance_management_gap.unit: program count among focused direct-service programs

population_context.value: approximately 21.2 million children through age 5 and 3.6 million births in the United States in 2024
population_context.unit: national demographic context cited by GAO; not a program-eligible denominator

recommendations.value: GAO made three recommendations: establish federal performance management for HHS Preschool Development Grants Birth Through Five, USDA WIC Farmers Market Nutrition Program, and VA Veterans Health Administration Maternity Care Coordinator Program

beneficiary_outcome.value: not observed as a linked family path from program contact through service receipt, developmental or health outcome, burden, correction, trust, or later security

observations.method: GAO identified 250 potentially relevant programs primarily from SAM.gov assistance listings, verified the inventory and collected information through a data collection instrument sent to 18 federal agencies, reviewed agency documentation, and interviewed officials as appropriate.
observations.uncertainty: The program inventory includes programs serving other populations and tax expenditures; the 15 focused programs are not the same universe as the 242 programs. Coordination is reported by officials and does not measure whether families experience seamless access. Performance-management status is a federal governance measure, not evidence of service effectiveness or failure.
observations.subgroup: Pregnant women, children through age 5, and their families; federal agencies and programs, including HHS, USDA, and VA programs named in the recommendations.
observations.counterinterpretation: State-defined goals can preserve flexibility, a small program may have limited dedicated performance-management resources, and programs can coordinate without sharing one outcome measure. Missing federal performance processes do not prove that services are ineffective or that beneficiaries receive no help; conversely, reported coordination does not prove improved outcomes.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO landing page and report metadata for the federal program inventory and recommendations.

boundary: This record establishes the scale, fragmentation, reported coordination, and performance-management gaps of a federal program ecosystem. It does not establish duplication, household access, service quality, child or maternal outcomes, causal harm, or political trust effects.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO report PDF reviewed; underlying agency data-collection responses and documentation are not retained.
